messages:
julia (FinSaaS): Hey team — since yesterday we've been seeing streaming completions drop with a 504 after ~30s for a subset of users. Happens only when using the Node SDK v1.3.2 streaming client. Correlation ID: abc-57f3-94. Our app then retries automatically which causes duplicate partial outputs and extra billing.

Anna (CS): Thanks Julia — sorry about the outage. How many customers affected and is there a simple repro you can share?

julia (FinSaaS): Only ~2% of sessions but it's hitting our high-value customers. Repro steps: start a streaming chat with a large system prompt (~1.2MB) + few turns, then wait ~25-35s. Example curl works too: ```curl -i -N -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","stream":true,"input":"<large prompt>"}'``` We see edge returns 504 and the SDK attempts a retry which reconnects and gets a new completion.

Mike (Support): Copying logs and traces to triage. Can you paste the raw SDK logs (DEBUG) and the correlation id from the failed call? Also, does disabling streaming avoid the 504?

julia (FinSaaS): DEBUG log snippet attached inline: ```[2026-03-16T12:04:21.345Z] request_id=abc-57f3-94 send: headers: {":method":"POST", ":path":"/v1/generate", "authorization":"Bearer ***", "transfer-encoding":"chunked"}
[2026-03-16T12:04:50.678Z] request_id=abc-57f3-94 error: upstream_read_timeout from edge, status=504
[2026-03-16T12:04:50.679Z] sdk retrying request (attempt 1)``` Disabling streaming (stream=false) the request completes fine but latency is higher and not acceptable for the customer UX.

Sam (Oncall): @Mike can you check if this looks like the 30s idle/keepalive edge timeout (we have a default connection idle at 30s for certain proxies)? Also check HTTP/2 stream window vs upstream behavior.

edge-bot: Trace: https://traces.internal/redwood/trace/abc-57f3-94 (logs attached). Key excerpt: ```edge: upstream_latency_ms=30205 upstream_status=504 backend_addr=10.50.11.3:8080 request_headers="transfer-encoding: chunked, user-agent: NodeSDK/1.3.2" backend_body_bytes=0```

Mike (Support): Looks like upstream closed after ~30.2s with no body forwarded. Two hypotheses: 1) backend runtime is hitting a read deadline when client hasn't sent more chunks (large initial prompt with streaming might lead to idle between initial handshake and token emission). 2) HTTP/2 FLOW control mismatch causing the backend to think stream is stalled. Temporary mitigation: set SDK to use non-multiplexed connections or increase the client keepalive and avoid very large single system prompts. For Node SDK you can try: ```process.env.DISABLE_HTTP2=true; // or set SDK option http2: false```

julia (FinSaaS): Trying DISABLE_HTTP2 now, will report back. Also attaching the sample payload we used (sanitized).

Anna (CS): I'll notify the customer success lead and flag as P1 for the impacted accounts until we have a confirmed mitigation. @Sam will you open an eng-runtime ticket to look for read-deadline/streaming regressions post-1.3.0?

Sam (Oncall): Opening ENG-1427: investigate stream 504s with large initial prompts + http2 multiplexing. Assigning to @eng-runtime. In the meantime, @julia can you confirm if setting DISABLE_HTTP2 reduced the failure rate?

julia (FinSaaS): Quick update — after disabling HTTP/2 the same flows completed successfully for 10/10 attempts in my smoke test. Error rate dropped to 0 in the test batch. Will run wider canary over next hour. :thumbsup:

Mike (Support): Great — marking workaround communicated. We'll keep this thread open while eng digs in and we run canary. If you see any new correlation ids, drop them here and we'll attach to ENG-1427.

Anna (CS): I'll draft a customer-facing note: explain temporary workaround (disable http2 via SDK env), reassure we're working on a permanent fix, and offer to roll them back once resolved.

edge-bot: Status update: ENG triage scheduled, trace samples uploaded to ENG-1427, priority high.

Sam (Oncall): Thanks everyone. Closing interim support loop for now — we'll post ENG updates here.

julia (FinSaaS): Thanks team, appreciate the fast turnaround.
